ei.title: Active Technological Metaphors and Passive Linguistic Metaphors
ei.subject: 올림포스전국연합고1_2026

fullPassage: Digital technologies are essentially related to metaphors, but digital metaphors are different from linguistic ones in important ways. Linguistic metaphors are passive, in the sense that the audience needs to choose to actively enter the world proposed by metaphor. In the Shakespearean metaphor "time is a beggar," the audience is unlikely to understand the metaphor without cognitive effort and without further engaging Shakespeare's prose. Technological metaphors, on the other hand, are active (and often imposing) in the sense that they are realized in digital artifacts that are actively doing things, forcefully changing a user's meaning horizon. Technological creators cannot generally afford to require their potential audience to wonder how the metaphor works; normally the selling point is that the usefulness of the technology is obvious at first glance. Shakespeare, on the other hand, is beloved in part because the meaning of his works is not immediately obvious and requires some thought on the part of the audience.

questions.passage: Digital technologies are (A)[essentially / rarely] related to metaphors, but digital metaphors are (B)[identical / different] from linguistic ones in important ways. Linguistic metaphors are (C)[dynamic / passive], in the sense that the audience needs to choose to actively enter the world proposed by metaphor. In the Shakespearean metaphor "time is a beggar," the audience is unlikely to understand the metaphor without cognitive effort and without further engaging Shakespeare's prose. Technological metaphors, on the other hand, are active (and often imposing) in the sense that they are realized in digital artifacts that are actively doing things, forcefully changing a user's meaning horizon. Technological creators cannot generally afford to require their potential audience to wonder how the metaphor works; normally the selling point is that the usefulness of the technology is obvious at first glance. Shakespeare, on the other hand, is beloved in part because the meaning of his works is not immediately obvious and requires some thought on the part of the audience.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.analysis:
✅ ① essentially — different — passive: 원문 일치. 디지털 기술은 본질적으로(essentially) 은유와 관련되지만 언어적 은유와 다르며(different), 언어적 은유는 수동적(passive)이라는 맥락에 부합 ←정답
❌ ② rarely — different — passive: (A) rarely(드물게)는 '본질적으로 관련된다'는 essentially와 반대
❌ ③ essentially — identical — passive: (B) identical(동일한)은 '다르다(different from)'는 맥락과 반대
❌ ④ essentially — different — dynamic: (C) dynamic(역동적인)은 언어적 은유가 수동적(passive)이라는 맥락과 반대
det.tip: essentially related(본질적으로 관련) / different from linguistic ones(언어적 은유와 다름) / are passive(수동적)

questions.passage: Digital technologies are essentially related to metaphors, but digital metaphors are different from linguistic ones in important ways. Linguistic metaphors are passive, in the sense that the audience needs to choose to actively enter the world proposed by metaphor. In the Shakespearean metaphor "time is a beggar," the audience is unlikely to understand the metaphor without (A)[cognitive / physical] effort and without further engaging Shakespeare's prose. Technological metaphors, on the other hand, are (B)[static / active] (and often imposing) in the sense that they are realized in digital artifacts that are actively doing things, forcefully changing a user's meaning horizon. Technological creators cannot generally afford to require their potential audience to wonder how the metaphor works; normally the selling point is that the (C)[uselessness / usefulness] of the technology is obvious at first glance. Shakespeare, on the other hand, is beloved in part because the meaning of his works is not immediately obvious and requires some thought on the part of the audience.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.analysis:
❌ ① physical — active — usefulness: (A) physical(신체적)은 이해에 드는 '인지적(cognitive)' 노력과 다름
❌ ② cognitive — static — usefulness: (B) static(정적인)은 기술적 은유가 '능동적(active)'이라는 맥락과 반대
✅ ③ cognitive — active — usefulness: 원문 일치. 은유 이해에 인지적(cognitive) 노력이 필요하고, 기술적 은유는 능동적(active)이며, 기술의 유용성(usefulness)이 첫눈에 분명하다는 맥락에 부합 ←정답
❌ ④ cognitive — active — uselessness: (C) uselessness(무용함)는 기술의 '유용성(usefulness)'이 판매 요점이라는 맥락과 반대
det.tip: cognitive effort(인지적 노력) / are active(능동적) / usefulness of the technology(기술의 유용성)

questions.passage: Digital technologies are essentially related to metaphors, but digital metaphors are different from linguistic ones in important ways. Linguistic metaphors are passive, in the sense that the audience needs to choose to actively enter the world proposed by metaphor. In the Shakespearean metaphor "time is a beggar," the audience is unlikely to understand the metaphor without cognitive effort and without further engaging Shakespeare's prose. Technological metaphors, on the other hand, are active (and often (A)[imposing / yielding]) in the sense that they are (B)[hidden / realized] in digital artifacts that are actively doing things, forcefully changing a user's meaning horizon. Technological creators cannot generally afford to require their potential audience to wonder how the metaphor works; normally the selling point is that the usefulness of the technology is obvious at first glance. Shakespeare, on the other hand, is (C)[despised / beloved] in part because the meaning of his works is not immediately obvious and requires some thought on the part of the audience.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.analysis:
❌ ① yielding — realized — beloved: (A) yielding(양보하는)은 기술적 은유가 '강요하는(imposing)' 성격이라는 맥락과 반대
❌ ② imposing — hidden — beloved: (B) hidden(숨겨진)은 디지털 산물에 '구현된(realized)'이라는 맥락과 반대
❌ ③ imposing — realized — despised: (C) despised(경멸받는)는 셰익스피어가 '사랑받는(beloved)'이라는 맥락과 반대
✅ ④ imposing — realized — beloved: 원문 일치. 기술적 은유는 강요하는(imposing) 성격이고, 디지털 산물에 구현되며(realized), 셰익스피어는 사랑받는다(beloved)는 맥락에 부합 ←정답
det.tip: often imposing(강요하는) / are realized in digital artifacts(디지털 산물에 구현) / is beloved(사랑받는)

Technological metaphors, on the other hand, ④<u>are passive</u> (and often imposing) in the sense that they are realized in digital artifacts that are actively doing things, forcefully changing a user's meaning horizon. questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: 기술적 은유는 '능동적(are active)'이라는 맥락. passive(수동적)로 바꾸면 모순
det.analysis:
❌ ① essentially — 원문 일치. 디지털 기술이 본질적으로 은유와 관련된다는 맥락에 적절
❌ ② passive — 원문 일치. 언어적 은유가 수동적이라는 맥락에 적절
❌ ③ cognitive — 원문 일치. 은유 이해에 인지적 노력이 필요하다는 맥락에 적절
✅ ④ are passive — 원문은 are active(능동적). 'Technological metaphors ... are passive'는 기술적 은유가 수동적이라는 뜻이 되어, 능동적이라는 대비와 모순 ←정답

Technological metaphors, on the other hand, are active (and often ③<u>imposing</u>) in the sense that they are realized in digital artifacts that are actively doing things, forcefully changing a user's meaning horizon. Technological creators cannot generally afford to require their potential audience to wonder how the metaphor works; normally the selling point is that the usefulness of the technology is obvious at first glance. Shakespeare, on the other hand, is ④<u>beloved</u> in part because the meaning of his works is not immediately obvious and requires some thought on the part of the audience.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: 청중은 인지적 노력 없이는 은유를 이해하기 '어렵다(unlikely)'. likely는 반대 의미
det.analysis:
❌ ① different — 원문 일치. 디지털 은유가 언어적 은유와 다르다는 맥락에 적절
✅ ② likely — 원문은 unlikely(가능성이 낮은). 'the audience is likely to understand ... without cognitive effort'는 노력 없이도 이해하기 쉽다는 뜻이 되어, 셰익스피어 은유가 노력을 요한다는 맥락과 모순 ←정답
❌ ③ imposing — 원문 일치. 기술적 은유가 강요하는 성격이라는 맥락에 적절
❌ ④ beloved — 원문 일치. 셰익스피어가 사랑받는다는 맥락에 적절
det.tip: the audience is unlikely to understand ... without cognitive effort — 인지적 노력 없이는 이해하기 어렵다

questions.passage: Digital technologies are essentially related to metaphors, but digital metaphors are different from linguistic ones in important ways. Linguistic metaphors are passive, in the sense that the audience needs to choose to actively enter the world ①<u>proposed</u> by metaphor. In the Shakespearean metaphor "time is a beggar," the audience is unlikely to understand the metaphor without cognitive effort and without further engaging Shakespeare's prose. Technological metaphors, on the other hand, are active (and often imposing) in the sense that they are ②<u>realized</u> in digital artifacts that are actively doing things, forcefully changing a user's meaning horizon. Technological creators cannot generally afford to require their potential audience to wonder how the metaphor works; normally the selling point is that the usefulness of the technology is ③<u>hidden at first</u> glance. Shakespeare, on the other hand, is beloved in part because the meaning of his works is not immediately obvious and requires some ④<u>thought</u> on the part of the audience.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: 기술의 유용성은 첫눈에 '분명하다(obvious)'. hidden(숨겨진)은 반대 의미
det.analysis:
❌ ① proposed — 원문 일치. 은유가 제안하는 세계라는 맥락에 적절
❌ ② realized — 원문 일치. 디지털 산물에 구현된다는 맥락에 적절
✅ ③ hidden at first — 원문은 obvious at first(첫눈에 분명한). 'the usefulness ... is hidden at first glance'는 유용성이 첫눈에 숨겨진다는 뜻이 되어, 판매 요점(첫눈에 분명함)과 모순 ←정답
❌ ④ thought — 원문 일치. 셰익스피어 작품은 생각을 요한다는 맥락에 적절
det.tip: the usefulness of the technology is obvious at first glance — 유용성이 첫눈에 분명하다

det.korean: passive=수동적인 (청중이 스스로 선택해 들어가야 하므로 언어적 은유는 수동적)

❌ ② loud: loud(시끄러운)는 은유의 능동/수동 성격과 무관
❌ ③ colorful: colorful(다채로운)은 본문이 다루는 수동성과 무관
❌ ④ expensive: expensive(비싼)는 은유의 성격과 전혀 무관

det.korean: artifacts=(인공) 산물/인공물 (디지털 산물에 구현되어 능동적으로 작동)

❌ ① errors: errors(오류)는 능동적으로 작동하는 디지털 산물과 다름
✅ ② artifacts: 원문 일치. 기술적 은유가 능동적으로 작동하는 디지털 산물(artifacts)에 구현된다는 맥락에 부합 ←정답

❌ ④ delays: delays(지연)는 작동하는 산물과 무관

questions.passage: Digital technologies are essentially related to metaphors, but digital metaphors are different from linguistic ones in important ways. Linguistic metaphors are passive, in the sense that the audience needs to choose to actively enter the world proposed by metaphor. In the Shakespearean metaphor "time is a beggar," the audience is unlikely to understand the metaphor without cognitive effort and without further engaging Shakespeare's prose. Technological metaphors, on the other hand, are active (and often imposing) in the sense that they are realized in digital artifacts that are actively doing things, forcefully changing a user's meaning horizon. Technological creators cannot generally afford to require their potential audience to wonder how the metaphor works; normally the selling point is that the usefulness of the technology is obvious at first glance. Shakespeare, on the other hand, is beloved in part because the meaning of his works is not <u>immediately</u> obvious and requires some thought on the part of the audience.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 immediately와 의미가 가장 반대인 것은?

det.analysis:
✅ ① gradually: gradually(점차적으로)는 immediately(즉시)의 반의어 ←정답
❌ ② instantly: instantly(즉각)는 immediately와 유사한 동의어
❌ ③ promptly: promptly(신속히)는 immediately와 유사한 의미
❌ ④ directly: directly(곧바로)는 immediately와 유사한 의미
det.tip: immediately(즉시) ↔ gradually(점차적으로). instantly·promptly·directly는 동의어

questions.passage:
(A) Shakespeare's <u>works</u> are still performed in theaters all around the world today.
(B) Technological creators cannot generally afford to require their potential audience to wonder how the metaphor <u>works</u>.
questions.stem: 다음 (A), (B)에서 밑줄 친 works의 의미로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: works: (A) 극장에서 공연되는 셰익스피어의 작품들(명사) / (B) 은유가 어떻게 작동하는지(동사)
det.analysis:
✅ ① (A) 작품들 — (B) 작동하다: (A)는 공연되는 셰익스피어의 작품들(명사 복수), (B)는 은유가 어떻게 작동하는지(동사)라는 뜻으로 다의어의 두 의미를 올바르게 연결 ←정답
❌ ② (A) 공장 — (B) 작동하다: (A)의 works는 공장이 아닌 작품들
❌ ③ (A) 작품들 — (B) 노동: (B)의 works는 노동(명사)이 아닌 작동하다(동사)
❌ ④ (A) 효과가 있다 — (B) 작품들: (A)는 동사가 아닌 명사 작품들, (B)는 명사가 아닌 동사
det.tip: works: ① (명사) 작품들 ② (명사, works) 공장 ③ (동사) 작동하다/효과가 있다

questions.stem: 다음 영영 정의에 해당하는 단어로 가장 적절한 것은? "ordinary written or spoken language, in contrast to poetry"

det.analysis:
❌ ① metaphor: metaphor(은유)는 비유 표현이지 시와 대비되는 산문이 아님
✅ ② prose: prose(산문)는 시(poetry)와 대비되는 평범한 글/말로 영영 정의와 정확히 일치 ←정답
❌ ③ horizon: horizon(지평/시야)은 글의 종류가 아님
❌ ④ creator: creator(창작자)는 사람으로 산문과 무관
det.tip: prose = 산문. in contrast to poetry(시와 대비되는)가 핵심

questions.passage: Digital technologies are essentially related to metaphors, but digital metaphors are different from linguistic ones in important ways. Linguistic metaphors are passive, in the sense that the audience needs to choose to __________ (active) enter the world proposed by metaphor.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오. (영어로 쓰시오)

det.analysis: 'to __________ enter the world'에서 동사 enter를 수식하는 자리이므로, 형용사 active가 아니라 부사 actively가 와야 한다. 부사는 동사를 수식한다. active → actively
det.tip: active(형용사) → actively(부사). 동사 enter를 수식하므로 부사형

det.analysis: 'is not __________ obvious'에서 형용사 obvious를 수식하는 자리이므로, 형용사 immediate가 아니라 부사 immediately가 와야 한다. 부사는 형용사를 수식한다. immediate → immediately

det.analysis:

det.korean: afford to=~할 여유가 있다 — 기술 창작자는 청중에게 은유 작동 방식을 궁금해하게 '요구할 여유가 없다'
det.analysis:
❌ ① refuse to(~하기를 거부하다): 'cannot refuse to require'는 이중부정으로 의미가 꼬여 맥락과 안 맞음
❌ ② hope to(~하기를 바라다): 'cannot hope to require'는 판매 전략 설명과 어색함
✅ ③ afford to(~할 여유가 있다): 'cannot generally afford to require ... to wonder'는 청중에게 은유 작동을 궁금해하게 요구할 여유가 없다는 뜻으로, 유용성이 첫눈에 분명해야 한다는 뒤 내용과 부합 ←정답
❌ ④ manage to(간신히 ~해내다): 'cannot manage to require'는 '요구해내지 못한다'로 맥락과 어긋남
det.tip: cannot afford to require ~ = ~을 요구할 여유가 없다
